learning_outcomes.description: Explainthe role of digital health in supporting safe, effective and person-centred healthcare.
Analysethe domestic and international strategic, policy, regulatory and technological drivers influencing contemporary digital health systems.
Applyknowledge of digital health technologies and information systems to address healthcare challenges in diverse practice settings.
Critically analysehow interoperable health information systems and digital health data support clinical decision making, quality improvement and patient outcomes.
Critically evaluatethe opportunities, limitations and implementation challenges associated with integrating digital health technologies into healthcare practice.

Develop and communicateevidence-based recommendations for implementing digital health solutions to improve health literacy and healthcare outcomes using appropriate written and oral communication approaches.

assessments.task_description:
Task Goal

To demonstrate the understanding of the concepts presented in the weekly topics and to demonstrate the critical thinking ability to relate the course learnings into ongoing changing in the healthcare settings and clinical practice.

Submission Guideline:

We exclusively use the UQ e-learning platform (Blackboard).

Complete the MCQ quiz individually.

Read each question carefully before selecting your answer.

Select one best answer for each question unless otherwise stated.

Ensure all questions are answered before submitting the quiz.

Once submitted, answers cannot be changed.

Complete the quiz within the allocated time.

Submit your attempt before the deadline; late submissions may not be accepted.

Ensure you have a stable internet connection while completing the quiz.

Academic integrity policies apply. Students must complete the quiz without unauthorised assistance

assessments.assessment_title: Assessment 2: Digital Health Solution - Business Case
assessments.task_description:
Purpose

The purpose of this task is to critically analyse a contemporary healthcare challenge and develop an evidence-based Business Case recommending an appropriate digital health solution. Students will apply their knowledge of digital health technologies, analyse domestic and international strategic drivers, and justify an evidence-based solution that supports safe, effective and person-centred healthcare.

assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.task_description:
In this assessment, you will build on the Business Case developed in Assessment 2 and take on the role of a digital health consultant presenting to a healthcare organisation’s Executive Leadership Team.

Using the same healthcare scenario and proposed digital health solution from Assessment 2, you will prepare an evidence based implementation strategy. Your presentation should critically analyse the potential impact of the solution on healthcare delivery, evaluate the factors that may influence successful implementation, explain how its effectiveness could be measured, and provide a clear recommendation about whether it should be implemented.

You will communicate your proposal through an 8 to 10 minute oral presentation supported by PowerPoint slides. Your presentation should use contemporary evidence and professional language appropriate for a healthcare leadership audience.

Following your presentation, you will participate in a 5 minute question and answer session. During this session, you will be expected to clarify and justify your proposed implementation strategy, supporting evidence and recommendations.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeksFrom Week 1 To Week 4(27 Jul - 23 Aug)
learning_activities.topic:
Module 1 – What is Digital Health?

Covers Weeks 1 - 4 of teaching

Week 1: Introduction to digital health and health systems: Topic one will review the definitions of digital health and introduce the Australian healthcare system in the context of digital health.

Week 2: Evolution of digital health & informatics: Topic two will focus on the historical development and uptake of information communication technology, data and data exchange. 

Week 3: Underpinning of digital health: Topic three explores the factors underpinning digital health transformation of healthcare, i.e., 'what' the problems are and 'why' digital health may fix them.

Week 4: What drives digital health transformation?: Topic four will discuss the key aims and objectives of digital health.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeksFrom Week 5 To Week 8(24 Aug - 20 Sep)
learning_activities.topic:
Module 2 – Digital Health and Patient-Centred Care

Covers Weeks 5 - 8 of teaching

Week 5: Clinical decision-making & digital health (Review): Topic five explores the uses of digital health in clinical decision-making, its application in in-patient care, iEMR uses, and information systems.

Week 6: Telemonitoring and virtual care (Review): Topic six is an overview of contemporary digital technology and applications that enable independent living, ageing in place, in-home monitoring and rehabilitation in the out-patient care setting.

Week 7: Mobile devices and health (Review): Topic seven discusses consumer personal mobile devices, wearables and remote monitoring and how data can improve clinical decision-making, client engagement and health literacy. 

Week 8: AI technologies and personalised medicine (Review): Topic eight explores the secondary use of digitised health data for personalised medicine, data analytics to improve organisational efficiencies and workflow, machine learning applications for image-based diagnoses, and AR and VR-based rehabilitation therapies.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeksFrom Week 9 To Week 13(21 Sep - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic:
Module 3 – Population Health Goes Digital

Covers Weeks 9 - 13 of teaching

Week 9: Person-centred care (Review): Topic nine explores the importance of person-centred care, digital health literacy, its meaning, and its role in engaging patients and their communities in healthcare. It also discusses strategies for building sustainable health changes. 

Week 10: Integration and implementation: Topic ten discusses ethical, medical, legal and social considerations for implementing digital health technologies. It also explores system interoperability and design for efficient digital health implementation.

Week 11: Integration Strategies: Topic eleven explores sustainability, system interoperability, data privacy, security, compliance, and common reasons for the failure of digital clinical applications. It also overviews the funding system and economic evaluation of Australia's current digital health model.

Week 12: Global status of digital health (Review): Topic twelve compares and contrasts various countries' current global digital health adoption and emerging trends. 

Week 13: Review (Review): In the final teaching week, we will review the important concepts discussed throughout the course to assist in preparation for the final Assessment.
